title: Felix and the Crown
premise: Isandro Zhou, a runaway apprentice hedge-witch, discovers their own name and tonight's date in a century-old book of prophecies — and is pulled through a dying gate into Thornfell's other realm, where the long winter is the slow death of a broken covenant. Guided by Felix, a disgraced crown-sworn warden who was prophesied to betray them, Isandro must gather three shattered covenant-stones while dodging both realms' armies, who each want the stones for themselves. When Isandro learns the covenant can only be reforged by a willing sacrifice of royal blood, they must choose between saving Felix, who is secretly the exiled heir, and saving two worlds. In the end, Felix offers himself, but Isandro breaks the prophecy's letter by giving half their own witch's life-thread instead, sealing a new covenant that costs them their magic but leaves both alive to walk out of winter together.
about_author: A. M. Okonkwo is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. They write fantasy rooted in borders, bargains, and the people who live in the gaps between kingdoms.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Fleeing her mistress Hedge-witch Marisol through the Thornfell passes, Isandro shelters in a smuggler's cache and finds a prophecy book naming tonight's date and her own name. The emotional beat: defiant curiosity curdling into dread as the pages begin to glow.

chapters.title: Through the Falling Gate
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The book pulls her through a collapsing waygate into the mirror-realm of Thornfell, where snow falls upward and the sky is bruised violet. She is captured within hours by crown wardens. Emotional beat: terror masked with smuggler's bravado.

chapters.title: The Warden Who Should Have Killed Me
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Warden Felix Ashgrave interrogates the intruder and recognizes her from his own childhood nightmares of the prophecy — the one that says he will betray her. He lets her escape instead. Emotional beat: duty cracking against fear of fate.

chapters.title: Bargains in the Undermarket
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Hiding in the realm's black market beneath a frozen city, Isandro trades hedge-magic for passage and learns the long winter is killing both realms. Felix finds her — not to arrest her, but to warn her. Emotional beat: wary alliance over shared hunger.

chapters.title: What the Covenant Was
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. On the road to the first covenant-stone, Felix explains the broken pact: a king's blood sealed it, a regicide shattered it, and the stones scattered. He omits that his family was the royal line. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Stone in the Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They retrieve the first stone from a chapel sinking into a frozen lake, fighting ice-wraiths born of the dying covenant. Isandro's hedge-magic resonates with the stone impossibly. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by the question of why her.

chapters.title: Marisol's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A vision from the stone reveals Marisol knew about the prophecy all along and trained Isandro deliberately as a vessel. Betrayal compounds betrayal. Emotional beat: rage that hardens into determination to choose her own path.

chapters.title: The Queen's Hunters
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The usurper Queen Vess's hunters corner them at a border shrine; Felix kills a former brother-in-arms to save Isandro, burning his last bridge to the crown. Emotional beat: grief transformed into open rebellion.

chapters.title: A Night Without Snow
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Sheltering in a shepherd's bothy, the two share truths: Felix admits he was prophesied to betray her; Isandro admits she ran because Marisol planned to use her. First kiss, quickly regretted. Emotional beat: tenderness at war with self-protection.

chapters.title: The Second Stone Sings
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The second stone lies in a war-camp amphitheater where both realms' armies now parley. They steal it mid-song during a truce feast, Isandro disguised as a court witch. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling when the stone whispers Felix's true name.

chapters.title: Heir of Ash
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Confronted, Felix confesses he is the exiled heir whose ancestors broke the covenant — the royal blood the reforging demands. Isandro feels the prophecy closing around them like a trap. Emotional beat: heartbreak braided with fury.

chapters.title: Split Roads
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix tries to leave alone to bargain his life to Queen Vess; Isandro follows him across the White Waste against a blizzard that is the winter itself, hunting them. Emotional beat: stubborn love refusing to let sacrifice be simple.

chapters.title: The Winter Has Teeth
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The personified Winter attacks, offering Isandro a deal: deliver Felix's blood and she may go home unharmed. She refuses and loses her sledge, supplies, and nearly Felix. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal and personal.

chapters.title: Marisol at the Gate
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Marisol crosses through a stabilized waygate with the third stone, offering reconciliation and a plan that requires Felix's death exactly as written. Isandro steals the stone and runs from her mentor a second time. Emotional beat: choosing found loyalty over old obedience.

chapters.title: Queen Vess's Court
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Captured and brought before Vess, Felix learns she engineered the regicide a century ago through time-bent magic and wants the stones to rule a frozen eternal kingdom. Emotional beat: cold clarity about the true enemy.

chapters.title: The Rescue That Proves the Prophecy
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro infiltrates the citadel to free Felix, but the rescue goes wrong exactly as the prophecy foretold — her actions hand Vess the second stone. Emotional beat: despair as fate seems self-fulfilling.

chapters.title: Betrayal, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The prophecy's 'betrayal' is revealed: Felix betrays not Isandro but Vess, publicly renouncing his claim and shattering her legitimacy before the assembled wardens. Civil war ignites inside the citadel. Emotional beat: liberation through redefining fate.

chapters.title: The Altar of Both Realms
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the original covenant altar, straddling both worlds, Isandro assembles the stones while Vess and Marisol converge. The ritual demands willing royal blood; Felix steps forward without hesitation. Emotional beat: love against duty at its sharpest edge.

chapters.title: Half a Life Given
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro interrupts the sacrifice, splicing half her own witch's life-thread into the rite so neither dies whole nor wholly. The covenant reforges on shared cost instead of royal blood. Emotional beat: transcendence through defiance of the prophecy's letter.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Ends
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Vess, unmade by the new covenant's terms, dissolves into thaw-water; Marisol departs without forgiveness, only a grudging nod. Snow falls downward for the first time in a century. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving peace.

chapters.title: A Witch With No Magic
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Powerless for the first time since childhood, Isandro grieves the loss of her craft and wonders if Felix loves her or the sacrifice she made. A quiet scene of rebuilding trust, word by word. Emotional beat: vulnerability accepted rather than hidden.

chapters.title: Two Roads, One Map
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Spring returns to both realms; the waygates reopen under joint wardenship. Felix offers Isandro a place at his side rebuilding the covenant's order — not as prophecy, but as choice. They walk back through Thornfell together. Emotional beat: home found in a person, not a place.
